turns.assessment: The service pattern is best explained by degradation of lightpath och134 rather than the common physical route: several services using S08–S15 are unaffected, while the affected services correlate with the BER increase at the S15 receiver. Normal receive power, estimated OSNR, DGD, and SOP rate make a power, amplifier, span, or polarization fault unlikely. A receiver-local penalty at trx.och134.a is most likely, but an upstream WSS filter shift can produce the same BER-only signature and is not excluded by the available monitors, so the evidence does not support an 80% commitment.

proposals.rationale: Pre-FEC BER rose at this receiver at t=606 while its receive power, estimated OSNR, DGD, and SOP rate remained unchanged. Receiver degradation directly produces this receiver-only penalty and explains degradation of services groomed onto och134 while other services on the same route remain healthy.

A shifted or narrowed WSS passband upstream of the S15 receiver could degrade only och134 with unchanged channel power and estimated OSNR. The listed scalar monitors cannot rule out this spectral penalty or identify a particular WSS.
Loss of margin on och134 could raise pre-FEC BER without affecting other lightpaths, but the abrupt level change near t=606 is less consistent with the documented slow decline.
